issues.title: Inconsistent spacing around function arguments
issues.description: The code contains inconsistent spacing around commas in function arguments that violates the project's rustfmt configuration. Specifically, missing space after comma and extra spaces after comma in method calls.
issues.rule_name: Rust Code Must Be Formatted According to Project rustfmt Configuration

issues.title: Cookie deletion incorrectly calls SetCookie instead of DeleteCookie
issues.description: The delete_cookie function is sending a WebviewMessage::SetCookie message instead of WebviewMessage::DeleteCookie. This causes the cookie to be set/updated instead of being deleted when the delete_cookie API is called. Any code attempting to delete cookies will fail to remove them, and may inadvertently persist or update cookies that should be removed. This breaks the entire cookie deletion functionality and creates a security concern where sensitive cookies cannot be properly removed.

issues.title: Window size applied before position in window_features causing incorrect window placement
issues.description: In the window_features method, the size configuration is now applied before the position configuration, reversing the original order. This can lead to incorrect window positioning behavior because some window managers calculate the final window position based on the current window size. When the size is set after the position, the position may be recalculated or adjusted incorrectly. This particularly affects windows opened through the on_new_window handler when both size and position are specified in NewWindowFeatures.

issues.title: Changed window naming pattern breaks window label consistency
issues.description: The window label format for dynamically created windows has been changed from "new-{number}" to "new-window-{number}". This breaks the established naming convention and will cause any code that attempts to retrieve or manipulate these windows using the expected label format to fail. For example, code trying to access "new-0" or "new-1" will not find the windows, as they are now named "new-window-0" and "new-window-1". This affects window management, event handling, and any window lookup operations that depend on the label pattern.

issues.title: Public re-export lacks rustdoc documentation
issues.description: A new public API item (`pub use tauri_runtime::Cookie;`) was added without a `///` documentation comment. Line comments (`// ...`) do not satisfy the rule requiring rustdoc comments for public APIs.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
// Remove this re-export in v3
pub use tauri_runtime::Cookie;
issues.rule_name: Public APIs Must Include Documentation Comments

issues.title: New code uses unwrap() on fallible operations
issues.description: Added code introduces multiple `unwrap()` calls on fallible operations (`parse().unwrap()`, `set_title(...).unwrap()`, and `build().unwrap()`), which violates the rule prohibiting panics/unwraps in favor of explicit error handling via `Result`.
issues.rule_name: Functions Should Return Result Types for Fallible Operations

issues.title: User-facing API change without a .changes entry
issues.description: This PR changes a user-facing API (renaming/replacing `with_window_features` with `window_features` and updating docs/examples accordingly) but does not add any markdown change file under `.changes/` in the diff, violating the requirement to include a covector change file for releasable functionality/API changes.
issues.rule_name: Changes Requiring a Version Bump Must Include a Change File

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14020 - fix: a few regressions from previous PRs

structured_output.summary:
The PR bundles three small cleanups from the earlier cookie and new-window work: drop a redundant `.clone()` in the runtime-wry cookie dispatch, restore the public `tauri_runtime::Cookie` re-export under `tauri::webview`, and move the API example's `on_new_window` handler into the desktop-only cfg block. It also renames `WebviewWindowBuilder::with_window_features` to `window_features`, reorders its size/position setters, and renames the example's created-window labels. None of the rename, reorder, or label changes appear in the PR description.

The cookie change is broken. While removing the clone, the author also changed the message variant in `WryWebviewDispatcher::delete_cookie` from `DeleteCookie` to `SetCookie`. `set_cookie` already sent `SetCookie`, so after this PR both public methods write a cookie and `delete_cookie` never removes one. The handler only logs errors, so nothing will flag it at runtime, and no test covers this mapping. The re-export restore and the example gating are correct. The rename is consistent across the repo, but the `window_features` body has rustfmt-breaking spacing that will fail a `cargo fmt --check` gate.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The critical issue is that `delete_cookie` now dispatches `WebviewMessage::SetCookie`, so the public delete API writes a cookie instead of removing it. This is a one-token fix, but it has to land before merge. The rest is minor: a rustfmt violation in the new `window_features` body, an unexplained setter reorder, and two small unmentioned example changes. The re-export restore and the desktop-only gating are good.

architecture.overview:
Apps call `Webview::set_cookie` and `Webview::delete_cookie` on the tauri crate (crates/tauri/src/webview/mod.rs). Those forward to the runtime's `WebviewDispatch` trait. In tauri-runtime-wry, `WryWebviewDispatcher` turns each call into a `WebviewMessage` and posts it to the event loop with `send_user_message`. The event loop's match arms then call the underlying wry webview's `set_cookie` or `delete_cookie`. Each cookie operation is a fire-and-forget message, and errors are only logged on the loop side.

This PR touches three seams. It restores the `tauri_runtime::Cookie` re-export so tauri users can name the cookie type without depending on the runtime crate. It renames `WebviewWindowBuilder::with_window_features` to `window_features`, which is the builder entry point for the `on_new_window` feature. And it moves the API example's `on_new_window` setup into a desktop-only cfg block, since `window_features` is compiled out on Android and iOS. The one runtime-wry change, though, swaps the delete path's message variant to `SetCookie`, which breaks the delete flow.
steps: Entry point: app code calls `Webview::delete_cookie` or `set_cookie` in crates/tauri/src/webview/mod.rs. These forward to the runtime dispatcher as `Cookie<'_>` values.

Runtime dispatch: `WryWebviewDispatcher::set_cookie` and `delete_cookie` in crates/tauri-runtime-wry/src/lib.rs (around lines 1699-1721) each build a `WebviewMessage` and post it to the event loop. The PR changes the delete arm's variant. This is the main defect.

Event loop: the match arms near crates/tauri-runtime-wry/src/lib.rs lines 3731-3741 map `SetCookie` to `webview.set_cookie` and `DeleteCookie` to `webview.delete_cookie`, so the variant chosen at dispatch decides the outcome.

Builder API: `WebviewWindowBuilder::window_features` (crates/tauri/src/webview/webview_window.rs, cfg-gated to desktop platforms) applies the new-window size and position. The PR renames it and reorders the size and position calls. Both calls are order-independent builder setters, so the reorder is behavior-neutral.
Example wiring: examples/api/src-tauri/src/lib.rs now registers `on_new_window` only inside the `cfg(all(desktop, not(test)))` block, which matches the platform gate on `window_features`.

findings.title: delete_cookie sends SetCookie, so deleting a cookie writes it instead
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-runtime-wry/src/lib.rs`, `WryWebviewDispatcher::delete_cookie` (around lines 1712-1720) sends `WebviewMessage::SetCookie`, so deleting a cookie writes it instead. Change that message to `WebviewMessage::DeleteCookie(cookie.into_owned())` so it matches the `DeleteCookie` handler near line 3737. Keep the `.clone()` removal, which is the intended part of this change. Leave `set_cookie` (around line 1705) sending `SetCookie`.

findings.title: rustfmt-breaking spacing in window_features
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/webview/webview_window.rs` inside `window_features` (around lines 1317 and 1321), remove the extra spaces in `inner_size(size.width,    size.height)` and add the missing space in `position(position.x,position.y)`. Run `cargo fmt` to confirm the file is rustfmt-clean. Do not change the logic.

findings.title: Unexplained reorder of size and position setters
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/webview/webview_window.rs`, `window_features` (around lines 1315-1322), the position and size blocks were swapped. Restore the original order (position first, then size) unless there is a documented reason for the change. The tauri-runtime-wry `position` and `inner_size` setters are independent, so the order is behavior-neutral. Keep the rename to `window_features`.

findings.title: Example label changed from new-{n} to new-window-{n} without explanation
findings.fixPrompt: In `examples/api/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, the `on_new_window` handler (around line 91) changed the window label format from `new-{number}` to `new-window-{number}`. This was not part of the stated intent. Either revert to `new-{number}`, or keep the change and call it out in the PR description.

findings.title: Redundant mut on AtomicUsize in the example
findings.body:
`created_window_count` is declared `let mut`, but `AtomicUsize::fetch_add` takes `&self`, so the `mut` is not needed. rustc will emit an `unused_mut` warning, and the move into the block is a good time to fix it. The base had the same `mut`, but this PR rewrites the line, so it is worth fixing here.

::code{file="examples/api/src-tauri/src/lib.rs" lines="74-78"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `examples/api/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, inside the `cfg(all(desktop, not(test)))` block (around line 77), change `let mut created_window_count = std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0);` to drop the `mut`. `fetch_add` takes `&self`, so the binding does not need to be mutable.

findings.title: No test guards the cookie message-variant mapping
findings.body:
The cookie methods in runtime-wry have no test that checks which `WebviewMessage` they send. The mock runtime's `set_cookie` and `delete_cookie` just return `Ok(())`, so a swapped variant passes every test. That is how the delete regression above got through. The wry dispatch needs a real webview, so a unit test is hard here. A lighter check is a small test that builds the message through a helper, or a comment on the variant mapping.

::code{file="crates/tauri/src/test/mock_runtime.rs" lines="645-651"}
findings.fixPrompt: Add coverage that `WryWebviewDispatcher::set_cookie` sends `WebviewMessage::SetCookie` and `delete_cookie` sends `WebviewMessage::DeleteCookie` in `crates/tauri-runtime-wry/src/lib.rs` (around lines 1699-1721). If a webview cannot be built in tests, extract the message construction into a small helper and test that. Keep the mock runtime in `crates/tauri/src/test/mock_runtime.rs` unchanged.

findings.title: tauri_runtime::Cookie re-export restored cleanly
findings.body:
The private `use cookie::Cookie;` was replaced by `pub use tauri_runtime::Cookie;`, which re-exports the same type that `Webview::set_cookie` and `cookies` already use. That keeps one `Cookie` name in scope, avoids a duplicate import, and matches the `tauri_runtime::Cookie` links in the docs. The `Remove this re-export in v3` note is a good signal for the eventual cleanup.

::diff{file="crates/tauri/src/webview/mod.rs" lines="19-24"}

findings.title: Example's on_new_window now desktop-only, matching the platform gate
findings.body:
`window_features` is compiled only for macOS, Windows, and the BSD and Linux targets. Moving the example's `on_new_window` handler, which calls `.window_features(...)`, into the `cfg(all(desktop, not(test)))` block keeps the example building on Android and iOS. The `on_new_window` method itself is not cfg-gated, so this is a case where the example, not the library, had to change.

::code{file="examples/api/src-tauri/src/lib.rs" lines="74-103"}

findings.title: Method rename has no stale references and matches upstream
findings.body:
`with_window_features` is renamed to `window_features` in the builder, its doc example, the webview module example, and the API example. A repo-wide search finds no leftover `with_window_features` references. The rename matches the upstream commit `b702058` ("rename with_window_features to window_features"). `on_new_window` is still pending in `.changes/on_new_window.md`, so no released API breaks. The PR description does not mention the rename, so a short changelog or PR note would help reviewers.

::diff{file="crates/tauri/src/webview/webview_window.rs" lines="1313-1316"}
